title: Schemes II: economy, farm and industry

questions.q:
With reference to PM Vishwakarma, consider the following statements:
1. It was launched on 17 September 2023 by the Ministry of MSME.
2. It covers 18 family-based traditional trades.
3. Any number of members of one family may register for its benefits.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; only one member per family (husband, wife and unmarried children) can register. Built on the pillars Samman, Samarthya and Samriddhi, it gives a certificate and ID, training with a Rs 500/day stipend, toolkits up to Rs 15,000 and Rs 1 per digital transaction. The 30 lakh registration target was met in 2026.
questions.s: SRI notes B9 (CA Sept 2026, Shankar pp. 12-15)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding PM Vishwakarma:
1. It offers collateral-free loans of up to Rs 1 lakh and then Rs 2 lakh at a concessional interest of 5%.
2. Artisans can register on their own through the Udyam portal.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 1 is correct; registration is only through Common Service Centres, followed by verification by the Gram Panchayat or ULB, a District Implementation Committee and a Screening Committee. The first loan runs 18 months and the second 30 months, with the government bearing up to 8% interest subvention.
questions.s: SRI notes B9 (CA Sept 2026, Shankar pp. 12-15)

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Scheme : Feature
1. BHAVYA : 100 plug-and-play industrial parks
2. Semicon 2.0 : Ministry of Electronics and IT
3. Mobile Phone Manufacturing Scheme : Successor of the PLI scheme for large-scale electronics
4. SME Growth Fund : Concessional working-capital loans to SMEs
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 1, 2 and 3 are correct. The SME Growth Fund (Rs 10,000 crore) gives equity through an Alternative Investment Fund, not loans. BHAVYA (DPIIT, Rs 33,660 crore) runs from 2026-27 to 2031-32; Semicon 2.0 has Rs 1,27,500 crore and the mobile scheme Rs 62,500 crore for FY27-FY31.
questions.s: SRI notes B9 (CA Mar, July, Oct 2026)

questions.q:
With reference to PM-KISAN, consider the following statements:
1. Eligible farmers get Rs 6,000 a year in three instalments.
2. It is a Central Sector scheme, fully funded by the Centre.
3. It was launched in 2019.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: All three are correct. PM-KISAN pays Rs 6,000 a year through DBT; by March 2026 over Rs 4.27 lakh crore had been paid in 22 instalments. Contrast PMFBY, the crop-insurance scheme of 2016, in which premium subsidy is shared with States.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana:
1. It replaced the National Agricultural Insurance Scheme and the Modified NAIS in 2016.
2. Premium subsidy beyond the farmer's share is shared by the Centre and States, 90:10 in the North-Eastern States.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Both are correct (static). PMFBY is a Centrally Sponsored scheme: farmers pay a capped premium (2% kharif, 1.5% rabi, 5% commercial and horticultural), and the rest is shared 50:50 by the Centre and States (90:10 in the North-East). In 2024-25, 4.19 crore farmers were insured. PM-KISAN, by contrast, is a Central Sector scheme.

questions.q:
With reference to the Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana, consider the following statements:
1. It was launched in 2015.
2. 'Per Drop More Crop' is its micro-irrigation component.
3. Its National Steering Committee is chaired by the Union Agriculture Minister.
4. It is a Central Sector scheme.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The National Steering Committee is chaired by the Prime Minister, and PMKSY is a CSS (60:40, 90:10 for NE/Himalayan States). Its components are AIBP, Har Khet Ko Pani, Per Drop More Crop and watershed development; it has created or restored 24.61 Mha of irrigation.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the National Animal Disease Control Programme:
1. Brucellosis vaccine is given once to male calves aged 4-8 months.
2. Eligible livestock are vaccinated against foot-and-mouth disease twice a year.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 2 is correct; the one-time brucellosis vaccine is for female bovine calves of 4-8 months, since the disease causes infertility and abortion and has no cure in bovines. Launched in September 2019, NADCP cut reported FMD outbreaks from 132 (2019) to 40 (2025) and tags animals on the Bharat Pashudhan portal.
questions.s: SRI notes B8 (CA Aug 2026, Shankar pp. 81-84)

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Instrument : Feature
1. Emergency Credit Line Guarantee Scheme : First launched in 2020
2. Startup India Fund of Funds 2.0 : Implemented by SIDBI
3. PM SVANidhi loans : Guarantee cover through CGTMSE
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: All three pairs are correct. ECLGS began in 2020 under Atma Nirbhar Bharat, and version 5.0 (2026) gives guarantees for West Asia crisis relief through NCGTC. FoF 2.0 (DPIIT, Rs 10,000 crore) invests through SEBI-registered AIFs rather than directly in start-ups.
questions.s: SRI notes B3, B9 (CA Jan, Apr, May 2026)

questions.q:
With reference to the Urban Challenge Fund, consider the following statements:
1. It is run by the Ministry of Finance.
2. It is a Central Sector scheme that funds the full cost of city projects.
3. At least half of a project's cost is to come from market sources.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 3 is correct. The UCF is a CSS of the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs: 25% of project cost from the fund, at least 50% from markets and 25% from the State or ULB. Its Rs 1 lakh crore is meant to catalyse Rs 4 lakh crore over FY26-FY31, with a credit guarantee sub-scheme.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Approval of Centrally Sponsored Schemes is aligned with the Finance Commission cycle.
Statement-II: Samagra Shiksha and PM POSHAN were given interim extensions in 2026 pending approval for the 16th Finance Commission period.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I; it is a consequence of it. Because schemes are appraised and re-approved for each FC cycle (here 2026-27 to 2030-31), schemes awaiting re-approval were extended to 30 September 2026. Budget 2016-17 introduced this alignment along with sunset dates for every scheme.

questions.q:
With reference to the Startup India Fund of Funds 2.0, consider the following statements:
1. It has a corpus of Rs 10,000 crore.
2. It is implemented by SIDBI.
3. It invests directly in eligible start-ups.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Like the first fund of 2016, it invests through SEBI-registered Category I and II Alternative Investment Funds, taking up to 50% of an AIF's corpus. It falls under DPIIT in the Ministry of Commerce and Industry and focuses on deep-tech.

questions.q: Which one of the following is not a feature of PM SVANidhi?
o: Cashback of up to Rs 1,600 for digital transactions
A free LPG connection for every registered vendor
questions.e: PM SVANidhi gives collateral-free loans, a 7% interest subsidy, digital cashback and CGTMSE guarantees, and links vendors to other welfare schemes through 'SVANidhi se Samriddhi' camps; it does not give LPG connections. States must have notified rules under the Street Vendors Act, 2014.
questions.s: SRI notes B3 (CA Jan 2026, Vision p. 98)
